picks.showTitle: Bishop Barron’s Sunday Sermons - Catholic Preaching and Homilies
picks.title: Love God—Not His Benefits
picks.summary: Friends for this Twenty-fifth Sunday in Ordinary Time, we hear a story from Jesus that tends to bother everybody: the parable of the laborers in the vineyard. We’re meant to hear our own voices in the complaint of these workers. Dealing with God, we often think things are unfair. Why does he do what he does? I’d like to get at this with a clarification that comes out of the heart of the spiritual tradition: You don’t fall in love with the benefits of God; you fall in love with God.
picks.reason: A homily on loving God for Himself, not for His blessings, from Catholic tradition.

picks.title: Holiness (Remastered)
picks.summary: The Language of Faith E1 —- Some of the most important vocabulary words in the Bible and Christian faith are rarely used in modern Western culture, or they’re used in ways totally different from how the Bible uses them. This short series qualifies, resurrects, and gives new meaning to three of these old terms. In this teaching, Tim explores the biblical word and concept of holiness, as it applies to God and people in the story of the Bible. Tim gave this message at Door of Hope Church in Portland, Oregon, on October 2, 2016.OFFICIAL EPISODE TRANSCRIPTView this episode’s official transcript.REF

picks.title: Fixing Gospel Contradictions: 2nd Century to Now
picks.summary: Around 170 CE, a Syrian Christian named Tatian noticed what a lot of readers have noticed since: the four Gospels don't always agree. So he fixed it. Tatian wove all four into a single, seamless account of Jesus' life. And for roughly two hundred years, in the Syriac-speaking churches of the East, that harmony was the Gospel.  Then the church came for it. Bishops collected copies and destroyed them. picks.reason: Discusses early Christian attempts to harmonize gospel contradictions and church responses.
